items.text: It is known. <break time="0.8s" /> That taking a photo of wildlife. <break time="0.8s" /> Requires a great deal of patience, confidence, and precision. <break time="0.8s" /> Yet the factor that many do not consider. <break time="0.8s" /> Is preparedness. <break time="0.8s" /> Before you face your animal subject. <break time="0.8s" /> You should study and learn about it. <break time="0.8s" /> So that you can anticipate its behavior. <break time="0.8s" /> For example. <break time="0.8s" /> Photographing the incredible migration of baby turtles. <break time="0.8s" /> From their nest to their new home in the sea. <break time="0.8s" /> May depend on luck. <break time="0.8s" /> If you want to get a shot of their momentous journey. <break time="0.8s" /> You ought to learn about them. <break time="0.8s" /> As much as possible. <break time="0.8s" /> Including the fact that they usually travel. <break time="0.8s" /> During the cool, dark nights of July. <break time="0.8s" /> Genuine knowledge about the animal you wish to capture through your lens. <break time="0.8s" /> Not only increases the likelihood of success. <break time="0.8s" /> But makes the slow time in the field. <break time="0.8s" /> Much more enjoyable.
